cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Be There for Me
cards.instruction: Get someone to show up, help, or stay involved as proof that the connection still matters.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've decided we're painting Dad's kitchen together. Since he died, I only see you when we empty a cupboard.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't I pay a painter? I can't face covering his height marks.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Covering them is not approved. You may help me tape around them instead.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll probably just sit on the floor and cry.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'm canceling the painting. You may cry here, beside me. I miss you more than I need a clean wall.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 decides the shared task, A3 forbids covering marks and grants taping, then A5 cancels painting and permits grief beside A, using authority to secure connection rather than labor.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 marks concern produces A3 preservation; B4 predicted crying produces A5 cancellation while retaining presence, a clear task-to-connection progression.

relationship.evidence: B2 offers payment and names grief; B4 honestly predicts inability to work, causing A to change the plan instead of belittling B.

heightening.evidence: B4 crying causes A5 to drop the practical reason entirely and grant the requested emotional space in company.

specificity.evidence: A1 deceased Dad and cupboard-emptying visits establish family loss; B2 height marks make the painting difficult in a specific way.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 canceling an entire painting session to permit crying beside A earns tender status incongruity from B4, not a joke at grief expense.
